items.description: The Colorado Plateau is a large desert region centered on the Four Corners area of the southwestern United States. It is known for its high elevation and deeply incised canyons, including the Grand Canyon.
facts: Covers parts of Arizona, Utah, Colorado, and New Mexico.
Characterized by its arid climate and 'red rock country'.
Contains the highest concentration of national parks in the U.S.

items.description: The Sierra Madre Occidental is a major mountain range system of the North American Cordillera that runs northwest-southeast through northwestern and western Mexico, and along the margin of the Colorado Plateau in the U.S.
facts: A major mountain range in western Mexico with extensions into the US.
Home to the expansive Copper Canyon.

items.description: The Chisos Mountains are a mountain range in Big Bend National Park in Texas. It is the only mountain range in the United States to be fully contained within a single national park.
facts: Located entirely within Big Bend National Park.
The highest peak is Emory Peak at 7,825 feet.
Its name is thought to derive from a Native American word for 'ghost' or 'spirit'.

items.description: The Olympic Mountains are a mountain range on the Olympic Peninsula of western Washington. They are not particularly high, but their sharp relief and heavy glaciation make them dramatic.
facts: Mount Olympus is the highest peak.
Known for receiving significant annual snowfall.
